# Summarise news quickly with Grok: Get the gist without the jargon

Ever feel like news articles are written in a secret language, or they're just too long to get through? This guide will show you how to use Grok, an **AI assistant** (a clever computer program that understands and generates human-like text), to quickly summarise news stories into easy-to-understand points. By the end, you'll be able to grab the main ideas of any article in minutes, helping you stay informed without the struggle. Please note that Grok cannot send emails, schedule appointments, or perform other actions beyond generating text summaries and responses.

## Before you start
- An active X (formerly Twitter) account.
- An active X Premium+ subscription, as Grok is currently an exclusive feature for these members.
- The X app on your mobile device or access to the X website on a computer.
- Roughly 5-10 minutes to follow along and try it out.

## Step 1 — Open Grok
First, you'll need to launch the Grok AI assistant. If you're on a computer, open your web browser and go to X.com. If you're using a mobile device, open the X app. On the left-hand side of the screen (or along the bottom menu bar if you're on mobile), look for an icon that looks like a stylised 'X' or 'Grok' text. Tapping or clicking this icon will launch Grok, bringing up its chat interface. If you don't see it, ensure you're logged into your X Premium+ account, as Grok is an exclusive feature for those members.
You'll know it worked when the Grok chat interface appears on your screen, often with a welcome message in the chat area, ready for you to type your first request.

## Step 2 — Start a new conversation
To ensure Grok focuses only on your new request, it's best to start a fresh conversation. Once you're in the Grok chat interface, look for a button or icon that lets you begin a new chat. This is often a '+' symbol, a speech bubble icon with a plus inside, or text that says "New Chat" or "Start New Conversation". It's usually located in the top-left or top-right corner of the screen, or sometimes as part of a sidebar menu. Tapping or clicking this option will clear any previous conversation history.
If it looks different, and you can't find a clear "New Chat" button, try looking for a menu icon (like three horizontal lines) or a gear icon, which might open a menu containing the option to start fresh.
You'll know it worked when the main chat area on your screen becomes completely empty, and the text box at the bottom is clear, with your cursor blinking, ready for you to input your specific request.

## Step 3 — Paste the news and give an instruction (prompt)
Now, find the news article you want Grok to summarise. For the most reliable results, copy the entire article text from your browser or news app. Paste this copied text into Grok's text box at the bottom of the screen. Immediately after pasting the text, add your instruction, also known as a **prompt** (your specific request to the AI assistant). Grok needs precise guidance to give you the best summary. While you *can* sometimes provide a web address (URL) for Grok to summarise, it's not always reliable, especially for articles behind a paywall; pasting the full text ensures Grok has all the information.
💬 Example: `[Paste the full text of the news article here] Summarise this news article about the recent weather patterns in Sydney into five bullet points, explaining any jargon.`
You'll know it worked when Grok starts generating a response in the chat window, usually appearing line by line above your prompt.

## Step 4 — Refine your summary
Sometimes Grok's first summary might not be exactly what you need. Perhaps it's too long, too technical, or doesn't focus on the specific details you're interested in. This is where refining your request comes in. After Grok provides its initial summary, you can simply type a follow-up instruction into the same chat box. Grok will remember the previous **context** (the article and your last request) and adjust its response accordingly. If it looks different, and Grok seems to have missed the point, try rephrasing your follow-up instruction more clearly and specifically, making sure your intention is unambiguous.
💬 Example: `Can you make that simpler, as if explaining to a teenager, and focus only on the impact on daily life?`
You'll know it worked when Grok generates a new summary in the chat, incorporating your feedback and presenting the information in a different style or with a new focus, appearing below your follow-up instruction.

## Step 5 — Ask follow-up questions
One of the great strengths of an AI assistant like Grok is its ability to engage in a continuous conversation. Once you have a summary, you can ask follow-up questions to delve deeper into specific points or clarify anything that's still unclear. This lets you explore the topic at your own pace without having to reread the original article. For instance, if the summary mentioned a technical term, you could ask Grok to explain it in everyday language. If you accidentally close Grok, your chat history should be saved, so simply reopen it and scroll to continue the conversation where you left off.
💬 Example: `What exactly does 'atmospheric river' mean in simple terms, as mentioned in the article?`
You'll know it worked when Grok provides a concise answer to your specific question, drawing details from the article you provided earlier, directly in the chat window.

## Common mistakes
-   **Pasting only the headline**: If you only give Grok the headline, it won't have enough information to summarise the whole story.
    *   **The fix**: Always paste the full article text for the best results, as Grok needs the complete content to work with.
-   **Vague instructions**: Asking "Summarise this" without more detail might give you a generic response that isn't tailored to your needs.
    *   **The fix**: Be specific in your **prompt**. Say "Summarise this for a 10-year-old," or "List the three main pros and cons," or "Explain the impact on local businesses."
-   **Expecting Grok to access private content**: Grok can't read articles behind paywalls or from your private documents, nor can it access content from a URL that requires a login.
    *   **The fix**: For paywalled articles, copy and paste the full text (if you have access) directly into Grok's chat window.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** You can quickly catch up on local or international news during your morning commute or lunch break without getting bogged down by details, keeping you informed and saving you precious time.
-   **For your business or work:** You can efficiently process industry news, competitor updates, or regulatory changes, getting the key takeaways instantly to inform your decisions without needing to read every lengthy report.
-   **If you're just getting started:** Pick any news article that looks interesting but a bit long. Use Grok to summarise it into three bullet points. See how much faster you grasp the main ideas!

## Try it now
Grab a link to a recent news article about something you're curious about. Go to Grok, start a new conversation, copy the full text of that article, paste it into Grok, and type: "Summarise this article in three sentences, making it very easy to understand."
